-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m1p4t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS N, Capacity

Teams == 0 .. (N - 1)

VARIABLES tokenAt, booked, crashed, tokenAlive

vars == <<tokenAt, booked, crashed, tokenAlive>>

Init ==
    /\ tokenAt = 0
    /\ booked = 0
    /\ crashed = [t \in Teams |-> FALSE]
    /\ tokenAlive = TRUE

PassToken(t) ==
    /\ tokenAlive
    /\ tokenAt = t
    /\ ~crashed[t]
    /\ tokenAt' = (t + 1) % N
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, crashed, tokenAlive>>

Book(t) ==
    /\ tokenAlive
    /\ tokenAt = t
    /\ ~crashed[t]
    /\ booked < Capacity
    /\ booked' = booked + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, crashed, tokenAlive>>

Release ==
    /\ booked > 0
    /\ booked' = booked - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, crashed, tokenAlive>>

Crash(t) ==
    /\ tokenAlive
    /\ tokenAt = t
    /\ ~crashed[t]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ tokenAlive' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, booked>>

Regenerate(t) ==
    /\ ~tokenAlive
    /\ ~crashed[t]
    /\ tokenAlive' = TRUE
    /\ tokenAt' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, crashed>>

Recover(t) ==
    /\ crashed[t]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, booked, tokenAlive>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Teams : PassToken(t)
    \/ \E t \in Teams : Book(t)
    \/ Release
    \/ \E t \in Teams : Crash(t)
    \/ \E t \in Teams : Regenerate(t)
    \/ \E t \in Teams : Recover(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BookingsWithinCapacity == booked <= Capacity
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    N = 3
    Capacity = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BookingsWithinCapacity
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler coordinates a set of surgical teams arranged in a token ring, numbered around a circle. A single scheduling token circulates around the ring, and only the team currently holding a live token may schedule work. The holder may pass the token to the next team clockwise, or, while holding it, book an operating room, which increments the count of currently booked rooms as long as the hospital's fixed room capacity has not been reached. Any completed booking may be released, decrementing the booked count. A team can crash silently while holding the token; the token is lost with it, and no team can schedule until the token is regenerated. Once the ring notices the loss, a live team regenerates a fresh token and takes hold of it. A crashed team may later recover and rejoin the ring. Throughout all token passing, crashes, regenerations, and recoveries, the guarantee is that the number of simultaneously booked operating rooms never exceeds the hospital's fixed room capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of simultaneously booked operating rooms never exceeds the hospital's fixed room capacity.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m4p6t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANTS Participants, MaxEpoch, MaxCap, MaxExec

VARIABLES sysEpoch, cred, queue, runner, capacity, executed

vars == <<sysEpoch, cred, queue, runner, capacity, executed>>

NoRunner == "none"

Init ==
    /\ sysEpoch = 0
    /\ cred = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ runner = NoRunner
    /\ capacity = 1
    /\ executed = 0

ReCred(p) ==
    /\ cred' = [cred EXCEPT ![p] = sysEpoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sysEpoch, queue, runner, capacity, executed>>

Submit(p) ==
    /\ cred[p] = sysEpoch
    /\ Len(queue) < capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, p)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sysEpoch, cred, runner, capacity, executed>>

StartExec(p) ==
    /\ runner = NoRunner
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Head(queue) = p
    /\ cred[p] = sysEpoch
    /\ runner' = p
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sysEpoch, cred, capacity, executed>>

FinishExec ==
    /\ runner # NoRunner
    /\ cred[runner] = sysEpoch
    /\ executed < MaxExec
    /\ executed' = executed + 1
    /\ runner' = NoRunner
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sysEpoch, cred, queue, capacity>>

Drop ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ cred[Head(queue)] # sysEpoch
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sysEpoch, cred, runner, capacity, executed>>

Rotate ==
    /\ sysEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ sysEpoch' = sysEpoch + 1
    /\ runner' = NoRunner
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, queue, capacity, executed>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ \E c \in 1..MaxCap :
         /\ c >= Len(queue)
         /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sysEpoch, cred, queue, runner, executed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Participants : ReCred(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : Submit(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : StartExec(p)
    \/ FinishExec
    \/ Drop
    \/ Rotate
    \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleExecution ==
    /\ (runner # NoRunner) => cred[runner] = sysEpoch
    /\ Len(queue) <= capacity
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Participants = {p1, p2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxCap = 2
    MaxExec = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleExecution
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler processes booking actions submitted by staff participants, but every action must be performed under current credentials. The scheduler keeps a system credential epoch, and each participant caches the epoch under which it was last credentialed; a participant is authorized only while its cached epoch matches the current system epoch. Participants re-credential to refresh their cached epoch. An authorized participant may submit a booking into a bounded work queue, but only while the queue has spare room, which supplies backpressure. The scheduler starts executing the booking at the head of the queue provided that participant is still authorized, moving it into the single execution slot. The running booking finishes only while its participant remains authorized. Periodically the security office rotates the system epoch, which immediately evicts whoever is in the execution slot because their credentials are now stale, and leaves queued bookings from now-stale participants to be dropped. The administrator may also resize the queue's capacity at runtime, never shrinking it below the number of bookings currently queued. The safety requirement is that the execution slot is never occupied by a stale or unauthorized participant, and the queue never holds more bookings than its current capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whoever occupies the execution slot always holds credentials matching the current system epoch, and the work queue never exceeds its current capacity.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m6p5t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Rooms, Teams, LeaseTime

VARIABLES lessee, ttl, phase, opsCount

vars == <<lessee, ttl, phase, opsCount>>

NoLessee == "none"

AllClosed == \A r \in Rooms : phase[r] = "closed"

Init ==
    /\ lessee = [r \in Rooms |-> NoLessee]
    /\ ttl = [r \in Rooms |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [r \in Rooms |-> "idle"]
    /\ opsCount = [r \in Rooms |-> 0]

Reserve(team, r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "idle"
    /\ lessee' = [lessee EXCEPT ![r] = team]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![r] = LeaseTime]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "reserved"]
    /\ UNCHANGED opsCount

Tick ==
    /\ \E r \in Rooms : ttl[r] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [r \in Rooms |-> IF ttl[r] > 0 THEN ttl[r] - 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, phase, opsCount>>

Expire(r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "reserved"
    /\ ttl[r] = 0
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ lessee' = [lessee EXCEPT ![r] = NoLessee]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ttl, opsCount>>

StartSurgery(team, r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "reserved"
    /\ lessee[r] = team
    /\ ttl[r] > 0
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "operating"]
    /\ opsCount' = [opsCount EXCEPT ![r] = opsCount[r] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, ttl>>

AdminOverride(r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "reserved"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "operating"]
    /\ opsCount' = [opsCount EXCEPT ![r] = opsCount[r] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, ttl>>

Complete(r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "operating"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "closed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, ttl, opsCount>>

Done ==
    /\ AllClosed
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E team \in Teams, r \in Rooms : Reserve(team, r)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : Expire(r)
    \/ \E team \in Teams, r \in Rooms : StartSurgery(team, r)
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : AdminOverride(r)
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : Complete(r)
    \/ Done

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StartedAtMostOnce ==
    /\ \A r \in Rooms : opsCount[r] <= 1
    /\ \A r \in Rooms : phase[r] = "idle" => opsCount[r] = 0
    /\ \A r \in Rooms : phase[r] \in {"operating", "closed"} => opsCount[r] = 1
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Rooms = {r1, r2}
    Teams = {tA, tB}
    LeaseTime = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT StartedAtMostOnce
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler manages a set of operating rooms, each progressing through the phases idle, reserved, operating, and closed. A surgical team reserves an idle room by taking a lease on it, which grants a fixed time-to-live and moves the room to reserved. A clock tick ages every live lease; a reserved room whose lease time-to-live reaches zero has its lease expire and reverts to idle without any surgery having occurred. While a room is reserved and its lease is still alive, the leasing team may start the surgery, which is the irreversible act: it records one surgery start for that room and moves it to operating. A privileged charge nurse holds an administrative override that can start surgery in a reserved room immediately, bypassing lease timing. Once operating, a room is eventually completed and moves to closed, where it stays. The critical guarantee is that surgery is started at most once per room: an idle room has zero recorded starts, and a room that is operating or closed has exactly one recorded start, so no operation is ever begun twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Each room records at most one surgery start, with zero starts while idle and exactly one start once it is operating or closed.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m0p4t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Requests, Runways, Capacity

VARIABLES state, snap, target, load, ver

vars == <<state, snap, target, load, ver>>

NoTarget == "none"

Init ==
    /\ state = [q \in Requests |-> "new"]
    /\ snap = [q \in Requests |-> 0]
    /\ target = [q \in Requests |-> NoTarget]
    /\ load = [w \in Runways |-> 0]
    /\ ver = [w \in Runways |-> 0]

Prepare(q, w) ==
    /\ state[q] = "new"
    /\ load[w] < Capacity
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![q] = "prepared"]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![q] = ver[w]]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![q] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, ver>>

Commit(q) ==
    /\ state[q] = "prepared"
    /\ ver[target[q]] = snap[q]
    /\ load[target[q]] < Capacity
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![target[q]] = load[target[q]] + 1]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![target[q]] = ver[target[q]] + 1]
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![q] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, target>>

Conflict(q) ==
    /\ state[q] = "prepared"
    /\ ver[target[q]] # snap[q]
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![q] = "new"]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![q] = NoTarget]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, load, ver>>

Release(w) ==
    /\ load[w] > 0
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![w] = load[w] - 1]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![w] = ver[w] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, snap, target>>

Done ==
    /\ \A q \in Requests : state[q] = "done"
    /\ \A w \in Runways : load[w] = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E q \in Requests, w \in Runways : Prepare(q, w)
    \/ \E q \in Requests : Commit(q)
    \/ \E q \in Requests : Conflict(q)
    \/ \E w \in Runways : Release(w)
    \/ Done

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LoadWithinCapacity == \A w \in Runways : load[w] <= Capacity
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Requests = {q1, q2}
    Runways = {rw1, rw2}
    Capacity = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LoadWithinCapacity
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator assigns arriving flights to runways using optimistic locking with retry, since several controllers act concurrently and their messages may be applied in any order. Each assignment request proceeds through the states new, prepared, and done. To prepare, a request optimistically targets a runway that currently has room below its capacity and snapshots that runway's version number. To commit, the request validates that the runway's version still equals its snapshot -- meaning no other assignment slipped in since it read -- and, if so, increases that runway's load, bumps the runway's version, and becomes done. If validation fails because the version has moved on, the request conflicts and rolls back to new to retry against fresh state. A landed flight may be released from a runway, lowering that runway's load and bumping its version. Because a request only ever finalizes an assignment after confirming the runway state it read is unchanged, and every commit rechecks room, the number of flights assigned to any runway never exceeds that runway's fixed capacity, regardless of how the concurrent messages interleave.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of flights assigned to any runway never exceeds that runway's fixed capacity.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m8p1t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Instances, Runways, MaxOps

VARIABLES coarse, fine, ledger, applied

vars == <<coarse, fine, ledger, applied>>

NoOne == "none"

RECURSIVE SumOver(_)
SumOver(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN applied[x] + SumOver(S \ {x})

HoldsAnyFine(i) == \E r \in Runways : fine[r] = i

Init ==
    /\ coarse = NoOne
    /\ fine = [r \in Runways |-> NoOne]
    /\ ledger = 0
    /\ applied = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

AcquireCoarse(i) ==
    /\ coarse = NoOne
    /\ coarse' = i
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, ledger, applied>>

AcquireFine(i, r) ==
    /\ coarse = i
    /\ fine[r] = NoOne
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![r] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, ledger, applied>>

Commit(i, r) ==
    /\ fine[r] = i
    /\ ledger < MaxOps
    /\ ledger' = ledger + 1
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![i] = applied[i] + 1]
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![r] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED coarse

ReleaseFine(i, r) ==
    /\ fine[r] = i
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![r] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, ledger, applied>>

ReleaseCoarse(i) ==
    /\ coarse = i
    /\ ~HoldsAnyFine(i)
    /\ coarse' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, ledger, applied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : AcquireCoarse(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, r \in Runways : AcquireFine(i, r)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, r \in Runways : Commit(i, r)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, r \in Runways : ReleaseFine(i, r)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : ReleaseCoarse(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LedgerNoLostUpdate == ledger = SumOver(Instances)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {x1, x2}
    Runways = {r1, r2}
    MaxOps = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LedgerNoLostUpdate
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator is served by two independent allocator instances that share one common pool of runways. To record an allocation, an instance must obtain a two-level hierarchical lock: first a single coarse airport-wide lock, and only while holding that coarse lock may it then take a fine per-runway lock on a specific runway. Holding both locks, the instance commits an allocation, which advances a single shared allocation ledger and the instance's own applied tally together, and releases the fine runway lock in the same step. An instance releases the coarse lock only after it has let go of every fine lock it held. Because both instances write to the same shared ledger but are serialized through the coarse-then-fine locking discipline, no committed allocation may ever be lost or double-counted. The integrity guarantee is therefore that the shared allocation ledger always equals the sum of the two instances' individual applied tallies.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared allocation ledger always equals the sum of both allocator instances' individual applied tallies.

VARIABLES pool, q, applied, ledger

vars == <<pool, q, applied, ledger>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_)
SumOver(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN applied[x] + SumOver(S \ {x})

AllQueuesEmpty == \A c \in Controllers : Len(q[c]) = 0

Init ==

    /\ q = [c \in Controllers |-> << >>]
    /\ applied = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ ledger = 0

Request(c) ==
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ Len(q[c]) < QCap
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ q' = [q EXCEPT ![c] = Append(q[c], "permit")]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, ledger>>

Apply(c) ==
    /\ Len(q[c]) > 0
    /\ q' = [q EXCEPT ![c] = Tail(q[c])]
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![c] = applied[c] + 1]
    /\ ledger' = ledger + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED pool

Release(c) ==
    /\ Len(q[c]) > 0
    /\ q' = [q EXCEPT ![c] = Tail(q[c])]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, ledger>>

Rebalance(c, d) ==
    /\ c # d
    /\ Len(q[c]) > 0
    /\ Len(q[d]) < QCap
    /\ q' = [q EXCEPT ![c] = Tail(q[c]), ![d] = Append(q[d], "permit")]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, applied, ledger>>

Done ==
    /\ pool = 0
    /\ AllQueuesEmpty
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Request(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Apply(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Release(c)
    \/ \E c, d \in Controllers : Rebalance(c, d)
    \/ Done

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {a, b}
    QCap = 2
    InitPool = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LedgerNoLoss
nl:
A subway signalling system controls train movements across a shared pool of track blocks. Two independent signalling controllers draw movement permits from one common pool of available permits. Each controller has its own bounded work queue: a controller may pull a permit from the shared pool into its queue only while its queue has spare room, giving backpressure once a controller is saturated. A controller applies the permit at the front of its queue to authorize a train movement, which commits the movement both to a single shared movement ledger and to that controller's own applied tally. A controller may also release the permit at the front of its queue back into the shared pool without applying it, and the two controllers may rebalance by handing a queued permit from one controller to the other. Because both controllers write to the same shared ledger, the integrity requirement is that no committed movement is ever lost or double-counted: the shared movement ledger must always equal the sum of the two controllers' individual applied tallies.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared movement ledger always equals the sum of both controllers' individual applied tallies.

CONSTANTS
    Blocks = {k1, k2, k3}
    Fleet = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FleetConserved
nl:
A subway signalling block system governs a fixed fleet of trains moving through a set of track blocks, where each block may hold at most one train. Trains start parked in a depot. A train can be dispatched from the depot into the in-transit pool, from which it seeks a block to enter. Entering a block is guarded by a compare-and-swap on that block's occupancy token: a train may enter only if the block's token reads free, and entering flips the token to occupied. A train sitting in a block may leave, flipping the token back to free and rejoining the in-transit pool. From the in-transit pool a train may return to the depot, or pull into a siding for storage, and a sided train may later re-enter the in-transit pool. Because movement authorizations travel over the signalling network and may be applied in any order, entries and leaves for different blocks interleave arbitrarily. Since trains are only ever moved between the depot, the siding, the in-transit pool, and the blocks -- never created or destroyed -- the total number of trains across all of these locations must stay constant.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of trains, counting the depot, the siding, the in-transit pool, and all occupied blocks, always equals the fixed fleet size.

EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes, Batch

VARIABLES leader, spooled, inProgress, printed, crashed

vars == <<leader, spooled, inProgress, printed, crashed>>

NoLeader == "none"

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ spooled = Batch
    /\ inProgress = 0
    /\ printed = 0
    /\ crashed = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]

Elect(n) ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ ~crashed[n]
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spooled, inProgress, printed, crashed>>

Fetch(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ ~crashed[n]
    /\ spooled > 0
    /\ spooled' = spooled - 1
    /\ inProgress' = inProgress + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, printed, crashed>>

Complete(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ ~crashed[n]
    /\ inProgress > 0
    /\ inProgress' = inProgress - 1
    /\ printed' = printed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, spooled, crashed>>

Crash(n) ==
    /\ ~crashed[n]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN NoLeader ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spooled, inProgress, printed>>

Recover(n) ==
    /\ crashed[n]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, spooled, inProgress, printed>>

AdminComplete ==
    /\ inProgress > 0
    /\ inProgress' = inProgress - 1
    /\ printed' = printed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, spooled, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Fetch(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Complete(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)
    \/ AdminComplete

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2}
    Batch = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT JobsConserved
nl:
A print shop runs a job spooler backed by several interchangeable spooler nodes, exactly one of which acts as the elected leader. A fixed batch of print jobs enters spooled and must all eventually be printed. When there is no leader, any live node may elect itself. The current leader fetches a job, moving it from the spooled pool into the in-progress state, and later completes it, moving it from in-progress to the printed tally. A leader may crash silently, which vacates leadership so another node can take over by failover; a crashed node may recover later. The shop manager holds a privileged override that can complete an in-progress job directly, without regard to which node leads, to clear a stuck print. Because every job is only ever moved one step at a time between the spooled pool, the in-progress state, and the printed tally -- never duplicated or discarded -- the total number of jobs across these three places must always equal the size of the original batch.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of spooled jobs plus in-progress jobs plus printed jobs always equals the fixed original batch size.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m2p6t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Branches, MaxEpoch, MaxInv

VARIABLES phase, vote, credEpoch, sysEpoch, inventory

nl:

To record a dispense, a pharmacist first prepares by snapshotting the current value of the shared counter into a private read value; the number of pharmacists that may be preparing at once is limited by a runtime capacity, providing backpressure. Holding a snapshot, the pharmacist commits with a compare-and-swap: the commit succeeds only if the shared counter still equals the snapshot the pharmacist read, in which case the counter is written to that snapshot plus one and the pharmacist's own applied tally goes up by one. If, instead, the shared counter has moved on because another pharmacist committed in the meantime, the compare-and-swap fails and the pharmacist retries, dropping its stale snapshot so it can prepare again. The pharmacy lead may change the concurrency capacity at runtime, never lowering it below the number of pharmacists currently preparing. Because the compare-and-swap prevents any stale write from clobbering a concurrent update, the shared dispense counter always equals the sum of every pharmacist's applied tally, so no update is ever lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared dispense counter always equals the sum of all pharmacists' individual applied tallies.

    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)

    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, enrolled, rejected>>

Recover ==

    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, enrolled, rejected>>

    \/ Seat

nl:
A university course-registration system accepts enrollment requests from students into a small set of courses, each with a fixed number of seats. Requests are buffered in a bounded registration queue: when the queue is already full a student cannot submit another request, which provides backpressure against overload. A registrar worker takes the request at the front of the queue and, if the target course still has a free seat, seats the student and increases that course's enrollment; if the course is already full the worker instead drops the request and bumps a rejection counter. The registrar worker can crash silently at any time, after which it processes nothing until it is restarted; students may keep queuing requests while it is down until the queue fills. When the worker restarts it resumes processing where it left off. The overriding guarantee, regardless of crashes, queue pressure, or restart timing, is that no course ever seats more students than it has seats.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of students enrolled in any course never exceeds that course's fixed seat capacity.
